newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB at five-month low on competition fears.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB at five-month low on competition fears.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc were among the biggest losers in the plummeting FTSE 100 index on Friday, dropping to a five-month low amid continued competition fears, traders said.
The stock was down 11-1/2p or 2.4 percent at 474 by 0900 GMT, its lowest since July, outpacing the 1.3 percent decline in the FTSE.
The UK government said late yesterday it would issue proposals before Christmas designed to allow rival broadcasters to gain access to digital television services.

"The draft regulations ensure that whoever establishes a population of set top boxes, all broadcasters will be able to gain access of fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms," said trade minister Ian Taylor.
Last week BSkyB shares dropped amid speculation that its launch of digital TV services planned for next year could be delayed.
Analysts also pointed out that relatively highly-rated stocks like BSkyB would be particularly vulnerable in a period of market turmoil.
BSkyB trades on a multiple of 33.4 times historic earnings compared with 15.5 times for the FTSE 100 as a whole.
